statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail. Let out_k(i,j) be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < n, (p < i or p > j), and nums[p] = k. For an integer v, let in_v(i,j) be the number of indices p with i <= p <= j and nums[p] = v. Then r = max { out_k(i,j) + in_v(i,j) : 0 <= i <= j < n and v is an integer }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= len(nums).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Let totalK be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < len(nums) and nums[p] = k. The function returns a result r and r >= totalK.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Let totalK be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < len(nums) and nums[p] = k. If totalK < len(nums), then the function returns a result r and r >= totalK + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Let totalK be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < len(nums) and nums[p] = k. Let M be the maximum of 0 and all numbers #{p | 0 <= p < len(nums) and nums[p] = v} for integers v with v != k. The function returns a result r and r <= totalK + M.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = len(nums).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50. Let totalK be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < n and nums[p] = k, and assume totalK >= n - 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = max { #{p | 0 <= p < n and nums[p] = v} : v is an integer }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50. Let totalK be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < n and nums[p] = k, and assume totalK = 0.

statement: The function returns a result r and there exist indices i,j with 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) and an integer x with -49 <= x <= 49 such that, after adding x to every element of nums[i..j], the number of indices p with resulting value equal to k is exactly r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: The function returns a result r and, for every nonempty subarray nums[i..j] with 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) and every integer x, if new_nums is obtained by adding x to every element of nums[i..j] and leaving all other elements unchanged, then the number of indices p with new_nums[p] = k is at most r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.

statement: Let count(v) be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < n and nums[p] = v. The function returns a result r and r >= max { count(v) : v is an integer }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies n >= 1 and n <= 100000. For every p with 0 <= p < n, 1 <= nums[p] <= 50. Also 1 <= k <= 50.
